answer: Proof-of-Work Ledge Registry. Each new identity must publish a hash whose low-order bits match a registry-assigned target, and the answer sits on a public ledge of recent solutions; a valid cipher ties each answer to the requester's nonce so copies fail. The target scales with total identities, so a clone campaign pays rising compute—roughly hours of GPU time per identity—plus forfeited umber deposits when stale submissions expire. Marginal clones run negative-EV.
